placements.why: The envelope's whole content — a spectrograph's calibration value stated and verified against reference plates — names an organizational-strategy category (instrument calibration) that nothing in the supplied empty strata covers. No existing strata entries exist to reuse, and the content is squarely about calibration as an organizational function (verification procedure, reference standards, instrument records) rather than opportunity, strategy, product, architecture, organization, proof, or templates work. This is a genuinely new, foundational category with no required parent.
placements.title: Observatory instrument calibration as its own organizational domain
placements.frame: What instrument, what calibration value, and what verification standard ground this calibration claim?

placements.title: Calibration claims are grounded in verification against a named reference standard, not asserted on their own
placements.frame: What reference standard or verification procedure is invoked to substantiate this instrument's stated calibration value, and does it hold across the full range claimed?
placements.why: All three expressions carry the same thematic content: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration is not asserted alone but grounded in verification against the June reference plates, holding across the full observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets) will keep feeding — the recurring practice of grounding a calibration claim in a cited verification standard — not a one-time fact itself; the specific frequency value and plate-date are position-grain evidence for this leaf, per the narrative grain test. No existing narrative leaves are supplied to reuse, so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
